title: Top 10 Countries Where iPhone Beats Android
hook: You'd guess the USA, but it's not even top five.

items.name: Saudi Arabia
items.line: Saudi Arabia just squeaks by at nearly fifty-two percent.

items.name: Bahrain
items.line: Bahrain goes iPhone with about fifty-three percent.

items.name: United States
items.line: The US? Just about fifty-four percent iPhone.

items.name: Switzerland
items.line: Switzerland sits right at fifty-five percent.

items.name: Sweden
items.line: Sweden hits about fifty-six percent iPhone.

items.name: Norway
items.line: Norway hits nearly fifty-nine percent, while neighbor Finland is about two-thirds Android.

items.name: Japan
items.line: Japan is about sixty and a half percent iPhone, while South Korea leans Android.

items.name: Australia
items.line: Australia is about sixty-three percent iPhone, while New Zealand is a coin flip.

items.name: Denmark
items.line: Denmark beats Australia by a hair, about sixty-three percent iPhone.

items.name: Canada
items.line: Canada wins with nearly sixty-five percent, almost two iPhones for every Android.

outro: Team iPhone or team Android? Tell me below.
description: Countries where iPhone (iOS) beats Android, ranked by iOS share of mobile web traffic in StatCounter Global Stats for September 2026. UN member states with over 1 million people.
sources: StatCounter Global Stats, mobile OS market share by country, September 2026
intro_topic: the countries where iPhone beats Android, by share of mobile web browsing

title: Top 10 Biggest Cities in the World
hook: Think Tokyo is the biggest city? Not anymore. Can you guess?

items.name: Seoul
items.line: Seoul packs about twenty-two and a half million people.

items.name: Kolkata
items.line: Kolkata beats Seoul by only about sixty thousand people.

items.name: Manila
items.line: Shoutout Manila, nearly twenty-five million people strong.

items.name: Cairo
items.line: Cairo, nearly twenty-six million, the only one outside Asia.

items.name: Guangzhou
items.line: Guangzhou hits about twenty-seven and a half million.

items.name: Shanghai
items.line: Shanghai has nearly thirty million people, and could reach about thirty-five million by 2050.

items.name: New Delhi
items.line: New Delhi tops thirty million, and it's projected to hit almost thirty-four million.

items.name: Tokyo
items.line: Tokyo, the old champ, drops to third with about thirty-three million, and it's shrinking.

items.name: Dhaka
items.line: Dhaka has about thirty-six and a half million, and may top everyone by 2050.

items.name: Jakarta
items.line: Jakarta is number one with nearly forty-two million people. Tokyo, who?

outro: Did your city make the list? Tell me below!
description: The 10 biggest cities on Earth in 2025, ranked by urban-area population in the UN's World Urbanization Prospects 2025 (UN DESA, November 2025). The UN's new method counts whole urban areas, not just official city limits, which is why Jakarta now beats Tokyo.
intro_topic: the biggest cities on Earth by population, counting the whole urban area

title: Top 10 Countries With the Longest Coastlines
hook: Think Australia or Russia wins? Not even close. Guess number one!

items.name: China
items.line: China's coast stretches fourteen thousand five hundred kilometers.

items.name: New Zealand
items.line: New Zealand packs over fifteen thousand kilometers of coast.

items.name: United States
items.line: The US clocks almost twenty thousand kilometers.

items.name: Australia
items.line: Australia, a whole continent, about twenty-six thousand kilometers.

items.name: Japan
items.line: Japan's thousands of islands total nearly thirty thousand kilometers.

items.name: Philippines
items.line: The Philippines, over seven thousand islands, about thirty-six thousand kilometers of coastline.

items.name: Russia
items.line: Russia has nearly thirty-eight thousand kilometers, and much of it faces the frozen Arctic.

items.name: Indonesia
items.line: Indonesia, with over seventeen thousand islands, hits nearly fifty-five thousand kilometers.

items.name: Norway
items.line: Norway's fjords and islands add up to about eighty-three thousand kilometers.

items.name: Canada
items.line: Canada wins with over two hundred thousand kilometers, the longest coastline on Earth.

outro: Which coastline would you road-trip first? Tell me below.
description: The 10 countries with the longest coastlines, using the CIA World Factbook's final (2025) edition. Norway's figure includes its outlying islands; coastline lengths vary with how they're measured.
sources: CIA World Factbook, Coastline field (final 2025 edition; Factbook discontinued Feb 2026)
intro_topic: the countries with the longest coastlines, measured in kilometers

title: Top 10 Most Visited Cities in the World
hook: Paris isn't number one. It's not even top five. Guess?

items.name: Kuala Lumpur
items.line: Kuala Lumpur welcomes about seventeen million international visitors.

items.name: Paris
items.line: Paris? Only ninth, with about eighteen million visitors.

items.name: Antalya
items.line: Antalya's Turkish beaches pull nearly nineteen million visitors.

items.name: Mecca
items.line: Mecca welcomes nearly nineteen million pilgrims and visitors.

items.name: Dubai
items.line: Dubai hits about nineteen and a half million visitors.

items.name: Istanbul
items.line: Istanbul gets nearly twenty million, down from twenty-three million the year before.

items.name: Macau
items.line: Tiny Macau, about thirty-three square kilometers, pulls in over twenty million visitors.

items.name: London
items.line: London is Europe's number one, with nearly twenty-three million international visitors.

items.name: Hong Kong
items.line: Hong Kong jumps to about twenty-three million, up nearly three million in a year.

items.name: Bangkok
items.line: Bangkok is number one with over thirty million visitors, about seven million ahead!

outro: Which city is on your bucket list? Tell me below.
description: The world's 10 most visited cities, ranked by international arrivals in 2025 from Euromonitor International's Top 100 City Destinations 2025 report (December 2025).
intro_topic: the most visited cities by international tourist arrivals

title: Top 10 Countries With the Most Olympic Gold Medals
hook: Think China is number two? Surprisingly, it's not. Can you guess?

items.name: Sweden
items.line: Sweden grabs one hundred fifty-one golds.

items.name: Australia
items.line: Australia punches above its weight with one hundred eighty.

items.name: Hungary
items.line: Hungary, under ten million people, has one hundred eighty-seven.

items.name: Japan
items.line: Japan edges Hungary with one hundred eighty-nine golds.

items.name: Germany
items.line: Germany racks up two hundred fourteen golds.

items.name: Italy
items.line: Italy has two hundred twenty-nine golds, just fourteen behind France.

items.name: France
items.line: France has two hundred forty-three, including sixteen won at home in Paris 2024.

items.name: China
items.line: China has three hundred three golds, tied with Britain, but fewer silvers.

items.name: Great Britain
items.line: Great Britain also has three hundred three, and wins the tie on silvers.

items.name: United States
items.line: The USA has over eleven hundred golds. Let that sink in.

outro: Who wins the most golds at LA 2028? Tell me below.
description: All-time Summer Olympic gold medals by country, through Paris 2024 (all-time medal table compiled from official results / Olympedia). Current countries only, so former teams like the Soviet Union (395 golds) and East Germany aren't ranked. Great Britain and China are tied on 303 golds; Britain is ahead on silver medals.
sources: All-time Olympic Games medal table, Summer (through Paris 2024): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-time_Olympic_Games_medal_table
intro_topic: the countries with the most Summer Olympic gold medals of all time

title: Top 10 Countries With the Most Time Zones
hook: You'd think Russia has the most time zones. Surprisingly, it doesn't.

items.name: Mexico
items.line: Mexico runs on four time zones.

items.name: Brazil
items.line: Brazil also has four, thanks to its islands.

items.name: Denmark
items.line: Denmark has four, thanks to Greenland and the Faroes.

items.name: New Zealand
items.line: New Zealand reaches five, counting its Pacific island realm.

items.name: Canada
items.line: Canada has five, since British Columbia stopped changing clocks.

items.name: Australia
items.line: Australia has nine, including the tiny town of Eucla's unofficial forty-five-minute zone.

items.name: United Kingdom
items.line: The UK has nine, with overseas territories stretching from the Pacific to the Mediterranean.

items.name: Russia
items.line: Russia has eleven, back to back, from Kaliningrad all the way to Kamchatka.

items.name: United States
items.line: The US also has eleven, but two cover only tiny uninhabited islands.

items.name: France
items.line: France wins with twelve, thanks to islands from the Caribbean to the Pacific.

outro: Which time zone are you watching from? Tell me below.
description: Countries ranked by how many standard time zones (UTC offsets) they use, including overseas territories but not Antarctic claims (France would have 13 counting Antarctica). Counts as of October 2026, after British Columbia's switch to permanent UTC-7.
intro_topic: the countries with the most time zones, overseas territories included

title: Top 10 Cities With the Worst Traffic Jams
hook: Manila or LA worst traffic? Neither even made the top ten.

items.name: Bangkok
items.line: Bangkok traffic adds about sixty-eight percent to trips.

items.name: Lima
items.line: Lima, Peru: about sixty-nine percent extra drive time.

items.name: Arequipa
items.line: Arequipa, Peru, hits sixty-nine and a half percent.

items.name: Bogotá
items.line: Bogota drivers lose nearly seventy percent extra time.

items.name: Lublin
items.line: Poland's Lublin surprises everyone at about seventy percent.

items.name: Pune
items.line: Pune, India hits about seventy-one percent, and it's not even India's worst.

items.name: Łódź
items.line: Lodz, Poland hits nearly seventy-three percent, worse than almost every megacity.

items.name: Dublin
items.line: Dublin hits about seventy-three percent, the worst city in Europe.

items.name: Bengaluru
items.line: Bengaluru, India's tech capital, hits about seventy-four percent extra drive time.

items.name: Mexico City
items.line: Mexico City takes the crown, with trips taking nearly seventy-six percent longer.

outro: How bad is traffic where you live? Tell me below.
description: The 10 most congested cities on Earth, ranked by average congestion level (how much longer trips take than in free-flowing traffic) in the TomTom Traffic Index 2026 edition, covering 2025 data (January 2026).
intro_topic: the cities with the worst traffic, by how much longer trips take
